system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: for each repair crop, the repair agent receives (i) design rule manual (DRM) images, (ii) the repair crop represented by a KLayout Python script, (iii) its DRV distribution, i.e., DRV type and location, and (iv) layer-wise skill files
system_prompt_style.note: Skill files evolve between iterations, so prompt content changes per iteration.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: The DRC repair agents are provided with the assigned repair crop and the DRV distribution of that crop, DRM images as visual cues for the design rules, and layer-based skill files
env_context_strategy.note: Context injected up front (crop script, DRV list, skills) plus tool-driven exploration via preview tools.

observation_format.evidence_quote: DRM images as visual cues for the design rules
observation_format.note: Images are input cues; tools return textual reports such as "new DRVs with bounding boxes".

tool_call_format.note: Repair operations expressed as JSON objects; tool-call mechanism not described.

tool_count.evidence_quote: three preview tools in Table 2 are provided to each repair agent

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: Class Object type Operation Applicable scope
edit_primitive.note: No file editing; edits are layout geometry operations (move_via, resize, add_polygon).

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote: Table 2: Preview tools available during repair.
tool_schema_source.note: Tools defined by the authors in the framework; no schema generation described.

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: three preview tools in Table 2 are provided to each repair agent
protocol_standardization.note: No mention of MCP or other agent protocols anywhere in the paper.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: it follows the ReAct paradigm and internally executes the four-role workflow: a planner, an adversarial plan reviewer, a DRC engineer, and a patch reviewer
loop_primitives.note: Iterative repair with DRC re-run feedback and up to five iterations.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: a planner, an adversarial plan reviewer, a DRC engineer, and a patch reviewer
planning_granularity.note: Planner role exists but no stored structured plan object described.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: EvoDRC decomposes the layout into bounded repair regions and assigns an LLM repair agent to each region.
multi_agent_topology.note: Framework dispatches one repair agent per crop plus Skill Refiner, DB Summarizer, Skill Judge agents.

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: DRC repair agents are dispatched to work on each repair crop

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: There’s no runtime limitation for agents to repair DRC, a repair task completes when the agent submits its final repair operation list.
human_in_loop.note: No human approval step described; acceptance is script/agent-based.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: the Knowledge DB, which not only stores the skill files for all layers used in the agentic DRC repair process but also keeps the proposed repair operations and DRV distribution changes within the repair crop

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: Repair operations and their resulting DRV changes are stored in a knowledge database and used to evolve the repair skills.
long_term_memory.note: Layer-wise skill files transfer across designs; History directory stores past repair records.

state_persistence.evidence_quote: the Crop History directory preserves repair crop geometry by layer, crop, and iteration annotation, serving as a backup to replay the geometry of repair crops from previous iterations

self_verification.evidence_quote: The local DRC analysis tool can be used to run DRC analysis on the repair crop and show the DRV distribution difference
self_verification.note: DRC/connectivity checks are harness-run verification; adversarial plan reviewer and patch reviewer give self-critique; Skill Judge is an LLM judge.

retry_policy.evidence_quote: We allow EvoDRC to run for at most five iterations and stop early when the block reaches zero violations.

rollback.evidence_quote: EvoDRC accepts a repair agent’s final repair operation list only when it passes the full-design connectivity check.
rollback.note: Edits are validated before application rather than rolled back; crop geometry backups exist for replay.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: We allow EvoDRC to run for at most five iterations and stop early when the block reaches zero violations.
termination_condition.note: Per-agent: task completes when the agent submits its final repair operation list.

cost_controls.evidence_quote: $3.75 five-minute cache write, $6 one-hour cache write, $0.30 cache read
cost_controls.note: Prompt caching used; no token budget reported ("There’s no runtime limitation for agents").

timeouts.evidence_quote: There’s no runtime limitation for agents to repair DRC, a repair task completes when the agent submits its final repair operation list.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: Run DRC on the selected repair region in a sandbox for fast region-local feedback.
execution_isolation.note: "sandbox" means a local DRC run on a copy; no container/VM described.

filesystem_access.evidence_quote: Cropped metal stripes in the repair crop are restricted to elongating or shortening their open ends within the repair crop to prevent unexpected consequences in unseen regions of the layout.
filesystem_access.note: Scoped to the assigned repair crop rather than a filesystem.

permission_model.evidence_quote: These classes distinguish editable objects from frozen context and prevent a crop boundary from implicitly granting control over an unseen portion of the design.
permission_model.note: Editability classes plus connectivity check gate every proposed operation.

tracing.evidence_quote: Each record includes the repair operations on each layer and their corresponding DRV distribution changes on the same metal layer, preserving trackable results

replayability.evidence_quote: serving as a backup to replay the geometry of repair crops from previous iterations

eval_hooks.evidence_quote: We quantify DRC repair quality using % improvement in the net number of DRVs
eval_hooks.note: Evaluation uses the DAC26-DRC-Benchmark harness; whether the runner ships in EvoDRC's own repo is not stated.

guardrails.evidence_quote: the connectivity check tool can verify whether the proposed repair operation breaks net connectivity, which affects circuit logic, so such operations are forbidden
guardrails.note: Skill-file mechanical checks (source check, claim citation, ambiguity check) filter generated skill outputs.

target_domain.evidence_quote: EvoDRC, a skill-evolution framework for agentic block-level DRC repair
target_domain.note: Domain is EDA physical design / DRC violation repair.

open_source.note: "EvoDRC is available at [13]." but no licence stated.

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: We use Claude Sonnet 4.6 from Anthropic as the agent [ 26, 27] for all agents in the EvoDRC framework
model_agnostic.note: Only one model reported; agnosticism not stated.
